concepts.def: Anglo-Saxon system of compensation paid to victim's family for crimes; varied by social status of victim.
Period when over 200 offences carried death penalty, including theft of goods worth more than 5 shillings.
Punishment of sending convicts to colonies, mainly Australia from 1787; abolished 1868 after 162,000 transported.
Home Secretary who founded the Metropolitan Police; officers nicknamed 'peelers' or 'bobbies' after him.
Model prison built on separate system: solitary confinement with hard labour to encourage reflection and reform.
Hanged for murder despite Craig firing the shot; controversial case that fuelled campaign against capital punishment.
